docs.text: as a coastal Canadian, am still in complete awe of the great lakes. Like it breaks my brain. Mountains through vermont and the rockies are extraordinary. The plains are interesting in their own way but there really is too much of them

When Ontarians think of how stunning nature can be in this country, our minds too easily shift to the Rockies, or the BC/Maritimes coasts. They're incomparable, but there's nowhere else on this planet like the Great Lakes. The fact our greatest city has one as a coastline? Unreal.
You know who’s great at describing the very nuanced vibrancy of a Lake Superior port city that’s a mix of super left leaning nature lovers and super right leaning iron range families? Arizonans.
yep...all those greenhouses, huge ones, all along Lake Erie down to and past Leamington. We used to camp down there in the fall and load up on veggies and things.
Are these all still Great Lakes-adjacent? Yes. I know what's good for me! ; )

Also the assertion that non-slop aesthetics are relegated to wealthy coastal elites. The Great Lakes/Rust Belt, northern Plains/Rockies, Southwest, and Deep South all have iconic and beloved aesthetic heritage.

Yes. Also the most shallow of the Great Lakes, and generally warmer than the others. Stayed in Fremont Ohio last night, I should’ve gone a little bit extra and stayed in Port Clinton, that way I would’ve woken up on Lake Erie and had a nice breakfast there or in Marblehead.

I wish my arthritic ancestors had chosen somewhere *other* than the Great Lakes Basin to start a new life. We have the most absurd microclimate on the continent, second maybe only to some parts of Alberta. And no hot springs.
Sure feels like the Plains to me. Not enough snow or Great Lakes connections IMO.
It really is! I'm going to have Great Lakes and forests in my future but will of course miss the plains and mountains.
